final_model.name: Corrected Hybrid Lexical + Semantic Duplicate-Related Retrieval

completed_operations: MOD-010 Corrected Lexical Reconstruction and Final Controlled Comparison

final_evidence.mod009_original: Original hybrid artifact retained as non-final due lexical representation mismatch
final_evidence.mod010_corrected: Corrected hybrid with exact MOD-004 lexical reconciliation

limitations: T6 is duplicate-related ticket retrieval, not unrestricted generic similarity retrieval.
The retrieval target is based on subsequently observed Dupe-of relationships.
Observable non-positive candidates are not treated as true negatives.
The evaluation measures ranking/retrieval performance within the frozen 101-candidate candidate pools.
The evaluation does not establish exhaustive open-world retrieval performance.
The evaluation does not establish reliable retrieval for candidates outside the frozen candidate-pool construction.
The system should not be interpreted as guaranteeing duplicate identification.
Retrieval output is a decision-support signal and does not by itself justify autonomous routing or human-review removal.
Ranking scores are not calibrated probabilities and no candidate-level probability interpretation is established.
No automation threshold has been established.
explicit_exclusions: No binary-classification interpretation of observable_non_positive was used.
No target-ticket pairing claim was made for missing target IDs.
No post-Creation query information was used.
No current/final Dupe-of field was used as a feature.
No post-Creation administrative fields were used as prediction features.
No evaluation-based semantic-weight selection was performed.
decision_statement: T6 is closed as a supported-with-limitations secondary decision-support retrieval capability. The corrected 0.50 lexical / 0.50 semantic hybrid is retained as the final advanced retrieval candidate because its lexical component exactly reproduces the frozen MOD-004 baseline and its hybrid weight was selected using TRAIN only. The frozen EVAL population shows the documented retrieval metrics. These results do not establish exhaustive open-world duplicate retrieval, autonomous decision-making, calibrated probabilities, or removal of human review.
